name: Alexander Shulgin
bio: American chemist and psychopharmacologist whose work ranged from industrial chemistry to psychoactive phenethylamines, tryptamines, and ethnobotanical pharmacology.

name: Bernardino de Sahagún
bio: Franciscan friar, missionary, linguist, and compiler of the Florentine Codex, produced with Nahua collaborators in sixteenth-century New Spain.

name: Claudio Naranjo
bio: Chilean psychiatrist, psychotherapist, and writer whose early work joined medical anthropology, psychedelic research, and experimental psychotherapy.

name: Garcia de Orta
bio: Portuguese physician and naturalist in Goa whose 1563 Colloquies recorded South Asian materia medica through direct observation and dialogue.

name: Gerardo Reichel-Dolmatoff
bio: Austrian-born Colombian anthropologist and archaeologist known for fieldwork among Indigenous peoples in Colombia, including influential writing on Tukano cosmology and yaje.

name: J. G. Soares Maia
bio: Brazilian natural-products chemist associated with INPA and Amazonian phytochemistry, including chemical study of Virola theiodora.

name: William Antônio Rodrigues
bio: Brazilian botanist associated with INPA, known for taxonomic work on Amazonian plants including Virola.

name: Pedro Ponce de León
bio: Spanish secular priest in New Spain whose brief anti-idolatry treatise recorded Indigenous ritual practices, divination, and uses of ololiuhqui and peyote.

name: Hernando Ruiz de Alarcón
bio: Seventeenth-century Mexican ecclesiastical judge and priest whose 1629 treatise on Indigenous ritual practice includes extended passages on ololiuhqui, peyote, healing, and divination.

name: Jacinto de la Serna
bio: Seventeenth-century Mexican priest and author of the Manual de ministros de indios, a guide for clergy that catalogued Indigenous rites, healing practices, and colonial anti-idolatry concerns.

name: Nicolás León
bio: Mexican physician, historian, bibliographer, and editor associated with the Museo Nacional, where he published colonial anti-idolatry texts in the 1890s.

name: Richard Spruce
bio: English botanist whose Amazon and Andes fieldwork produced foundational nineteenth-century descriptions of caapi, niopo, and other Indigenous psychoactive plant preparations.

name: Alfred Russel Wallace
bio: English naturalist and editor of Richard Spruce's Notes of a Botanist on the Amazon and Andes.

name: Diego Durán
bio: Dominican friar and historian of New Spain whose Historia de las Indias de Nueva España preserved Nahua historical traditions, ritual descriptions, and colonial interpretations of Mexica ceremonial life.

name: José F. Ramírez
bio: Mexican historian, bibliographer, and editor who prepared the 1867 publication of Diego Durán's Historia with notes and illustrations.

name: Manuel Villavicencio
bio: Ecuadorian physician and geographer whose 1858 Geografía de la República del Ecuador includes a notable Spanish account of ayahuasca use in eastern Ecuador and a first-person description of its effects.

name: Alexander von Humboldt
bio: Prussian naturalist, geographer, and explorer whose American travel writings shaped nineteenth-century science and included early descriptions of Orinoco niopo.

name: Aimé Bonpland
bio: French botanist and explorer who traveled with Alexander von Humboldt in Spanish America and co-authored the Personal Narrative.

name: Helen Maria Williams
bio: English writer, translator, and political commentator who translated Humboldt and Bonpland's Personal Narrative into English.

name: Johann Baptist von Spix
bio: Bavarian zoologist and explorer who traveled in Brazil from 1817 to 1820 and co-authored Reise in Brasilien.

name: Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius
bio: Bavarian botanist and explorer whose Brazilian fieldwork and publications became central to nineteenth-century Amazonian natural history.

name: Georg Heinrich von Langsdorff
bio: German-Russian naturalist and explorer whose voyage writings included observations from Kamchatka, Russian America, and Brazil.

name: Ralph T. H. Griffith
bio: British Indologist, educator, and translator whose late nineteenth-century English renderings of the Vedas made Sanskrit texts widely available to Anglophone readers.

name: Jacques-Joseph Moreau
bio: French psychiatrist, often called Moreau de Tours, whose 1845 Du hachisch et de l'aliénation mentale made hashish central to a clinical theory of drug-induced delirium and mental illness.

name: Ernst von Bibra
bio: German naturalist and chemist whose Die narkotischen Genussmittel und der Mensch surveyed intoxicants comparatively through botany, chemistry, travel accounts, and self-experiment.

name: Edward M. Kennedy
bio: U.S. senator from Massachusetts whose health subcommittee helped investigate CIA drug testing and human-subjects research in the 1970s.

name: Daniel K. Inouye
bio: U.S. senator from Hawaii and chair of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence during the 1977 MKULTRA hearing.

name: Frank Church
bio: U.S. senator from Idaho who chaired the Senate Select Committee to Study Governmental Operations with Respect to Intelligence Activities, commonly known as the Church Committee.

name: Nelson A. Rockefeller
bio: Vice president of the United States and chair of the 1975 Commission on CIA Activities within the United States.
